name: Oakley hamlet
notes: Training level A2 (D-59): a hamlet of five households round a green with a well. Fields as in data/maps/village.json.

art.ground: a village green of rough grass worn into paths between cottages, a muddy lane coming in from the bottom, daisies, a few chickens' scratchings and puddles

pieces.ReeveHouse: a long timber-framed farmhouse with whitewashed walls, a thatched roof and a door facing down
pieces.Cob: a small log cottage with a turf roof and a door facing down
pieces.Liss: a small whitewashed cottage with a thatched roof and a loom visible through a window, door facing down
pieces.Fenn: a tiny, crooked old cottage of wattle and daub with a sagging thatch and a door facing down
pieces.Well: a round stone village well with a wooden windlass and a bucket
pieces.Woodpile: a woodcutter's woodpile with a chopping block
pieces.Sty: a small pigsty of wattle fencing with a muddy floor

oak.name: oak tree
oak.description: The great oak on the green, where the hamlet meets on feast days.

after_arrest.words: see you off down the lane
